scope: Actual final-build native VRAM captures and separate pixel-exact raster/movement/keyboard tasks; agent review, not a participant usability study or native FPS benchmark.
findings: Clarity: original app/folder identities, consistent title controls, navigation buttons and independent appearance/accessibility states remain readable.

Convenience: ordinary title-bar movement remains direct; Escape restores the prior rectangle and visible viewport without accepting another action. A partly off-screen move intentionally retains a reachable caption.
User friendliness: keyboard-only routes, F1 current-control help and forward/reverse panes retain real owner/generation semantics and saved choices.

Graphical quality: default shadows keep their prior edges and antialiasing; the exact production raster and twelve native cached/full comparisons preserve output while removing covered interior iteration.

Readability: reviewed ordinary, compact Dark, high-contrast and physical 4K essential labels stay legible without new overlap or clipped active controls. The first-guide boundary remains distinct over Dark Files.
Resource observations separate the constant fixed shell, managed current/peak, zero completed retention and bounded host probe buffers; host timing is not display refresh.
